c.tagline: Karst-peak river town on the Li and Yulong rivers, China's backpacker and rock-climbing capital near Guilin.

taxi.fareNote: Metered in town, but for trips to/from Guilin airport or countryside villages a flat negotiated fare is common; few drivers speak English.

emergency.note: 119 is for fire; English-speaking dispatch is limited, so having a hotel staffer or Mandarin speaker call is helpful.

avoid.reason: Expect pushy touts, bar overcharging on West Street at night, and occasional scooter-rental deposit disputes.

hood_desc: Yangshuo's pedestrian tourist artery lined with bars, souvenir stalls, and guesthouses in restored Qing-era buildings; best for first-timers who want restaurants, nightlife, and Li River access within a five-minute walk.

The riverside promenade and park along the Li River just east of West Street, with cormorant-fishing demonstrations and sunset views; suits travelers who want a quieter base still close to the action.

A patchwork of rice paddies and limestone karsts along the Yulong River south of town, reached by bicycle or e-bike and dotted with farmhouse guesthouses and bamboo-raft docks; ideal for cyclists wanting rural scenery.

The area around Moon Hill's natural rock arch and the region's best rock-climbing routes, a short scooter ride from West Street; suits climbers, hikers, and those wanting mountain views over nightlife.
A slower-paced Ming and Qing-dynasty river town about 25 km north of Yangshuo, famous as the scenery on China's 20-yuan banknote; suits travelers seeking authentic village life away from the crowds.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Local buses and shuttles typically run roughly 6:30 AM to 9:30 PM; no late-night public transit.
transit.pay: Cash or mobile payment (Alipay/WeChat Pay) on buses; no rechargeable transit card system in Yangshuo.
transit.note: Yangshuo itself has no metro or extensive city bus network; most visitors get around by bicycle, e-bike, taxi, or bamboo raft, with buses and a high-speed rail station connecting to Guilin (about an hour away).

ferry: Li River cruise boats and bamboo rafts

car.idp: Not valid; a Chinese driving license is required to drive, so self-drive rental is uncommon for foreign visitors

tip.r: Tipping is not customary and can even cause confusion; upscale hotels or tour groups may add a service charge instead.

landmarks: Li River at Xingping
The karst-framed river bend printed on the 20-yuan banknote, best admired from a raft or the ancient fishing town's stone quay.
Yulong River
Punt down this serene Li tributary on a bamboo raft, gliding past rice paddies, water buffalo and centuries-old stone bridges.
Moon Hill
A limestone arch pierced clean through a hilltop; the 800-step climb rewards sweaty hikers with views over a sea of karst pinnacles.
West Street (Xi Jie)
Yangshuo's 1,400-year-old flagstone artery, now a lively strip of cafés, silk shops and beer gardens beneath neon-lit limestone peaks.
Xianggong Hill
Photographers' favorite sunrise perch, overlooking the Li River curling through layered karst towers as morning mist drifts between them.
Impression Sanjie Liu
Zhang Yimou directs hundreds of fishermen, lights and twelve karst peaks in this nightly open-air spectacle staged on the Li River itself.
Silver Cave (Yinzi Yan)
A multi-level show cave dripping with chandelier-like stalactites, its illuminated crystal palaces among Guangxi's most dazzling underground sights.
Xingping Ancient Town
A 1,700-year-old riverside town of Ming-era lanes and faded trading houses, gateway to the Li River's most famous scenery.
Ten-Mile Gallery (Shili Hualang)
A cycling road threading past Moon Hill and butterfly-shaped peaks, so scenic locals call it a ten-mile-long natural art gallery.
Big Banyan Tree Park
A 1,400-year-old banyan spreading beside the Jinbao River, legendary setting of folk heroine Liu Sanjie's love story and songs.

train.note: There are no international trains; the nearest cross-border rail is the Nanning to Hanoi service, several hours away by domestic train. Yangshuo's own high-speed station sits out at Xingping, roughly 30 km from the town, on the Guiyang-Guangzhou high-speed line, so Guangzhou is about three hours away and Guilin barely twenty minutes. Many travellers still use Guilin's stations - Guilin West and Guilin North - and there is a long overnight conventional train up from Shenzhen near the Hong Kong border, around 12 hours. Book on 12306 with your passport and budget 40-50 minutes for the shuttle bus or taxi between Yangshuo station and West Street.

bus.note: No international buses run from Yangshuo. The workhorse connection is Guilin: government express coaches leave roughly every twenty minutes and take about 1.5 hours for around ¥22, while cheaper private minibuses from the Guilin railway station square (80-90 minutes, around ¥18) are slower and prone to touting. Overnight sleeper buses come direct from Shenzhen and Guangzhou for roughly ¥100-250 depending on the departure terminal. Yangshuo's bus station is on Pantao Road, a short walk from West Street, and tickets are bought at the counter.

intl.to: Guilin (China) - Li River cruise boats from Zhujiang / Mopanshan piers, 4-5 hours downstream, landing at Yangshuo's town pier
intl.op: Guilin Li River tour boat operators — booked through hotels and agents in Guilin; no official English booking site

ferry.note: The classic arrival in Yangshuo is by boat down the Li River from Guilin, a 4-5 hour cruise that costs ¥400 and up on the licensed foreigner boats, or roughly ¥100 if you join a Chinese tour group. Boats leave in the morning only and dock at the pier in the middle of Yangshuo town. Sailings are reduced or shortened in winter and early spring when water levels drop, and can be cancelled outright after heavy rain. Shorter bamboo-raft trips run on the Yulong River and between Xingping and Yangdi as excursions rather than transport.
